correctness.rationale: Conserved outer-pair SU(2) Casimirs give exhaustive plus/minus energy branches and spin-multiplet multiplicities, summing to exactly 2^(2m+1). All nonzero-triplet sector minima occur at maximal composite spin, and the energy becomes affine in the number k of triplet pairs. Comparing k=0,1,m proves both critical ratios, exact degeneracies and gap branches for every m>=2. An independent computational-basis diagonalization matched all eigenvalues and multiplicities for 15 cases (m=2,3,4 and five coupling ratios), largest discrepancy 2.31e-14; finite checks supplement, not replace, proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: None of these Hamiltonians is a specialization or strictly stronger version of the present model: shared quantum-hub exchange cannot be obtained by parameter substitution from Ising-mediated inter-plaquette exchange, and a single outer triangle has three mutually bonded peripheral sites rather than the disjoint pairing pattern present for arbitrary m. Their exact results do not imply the claimed m2^m degeneracy and full gap formula.

value.rationale: The finite graph sequence is a natural family of corner-sharing frustrated spin triangles. Exact, all-size coupling-dependent ground multiplets show a collective spin collapse and an exponentially degenerate critical point with residual entropy (log 2)/2 per spin; the exact gap and whole spectrum are structural, not an arbitrary finite table. These are useful benchmarks for bond-frustration, molecular spin and numerical many-body studies, without claiming physical robustness or finite-temperature criticality.
